why: Expression cycle 15 (docs/v3/cycles/expression-15.md) lost 26 of its 48 round-0 points to lessons the kit could already do (class `skill`), one of them a P2 cause (n70 F6 .12: at 390 only 6 of 9 event names reach the x axis, where `x.tickFormat` from the cycle-14 Spec would name all nine). X1 (word economy) lost a point on 6 of 6 cases again, although every builder ran the fact count to an empty print on its final source and no builder said it printed a property name (cycle 14: 4 of 6): the repeats it missed are a value one helper prints into several parts (n69 'Fri 14:00' three times through `stamp()`), `Record` label maps (n70 `STATUS_LABEL`, 'waiting' four times; n72 `CASE_LABEL`), a state said by a zone caption, a pill and a sub line (n71 'Behind'), and a legend that repeats the axis titles. X2 (one view) lost a point on 6 of 6, the sixth cycle running: parts sized past their content (n69's heat card 540 px for 5 rows, n74's bars card 862 px, n72's forced `min-h-160`, n73's strip 226 px for one sparkline) and a 12-row list as twelve five-line phone cards where `phone: 'columns'` fits (n72).
what: Skill and rule text for the skill findings of expression cycle 15: a read-aloud pass the fact count cannot replace, parts sized to their content, and the single lessons the builders missed.
owns: packages/basalt-ui/agent/skills/** and packages/basalt-ui/agent/rules/** (through their generators where generated)
the dogfooded copies the repo syncs
must_not_touch: packages/basalt-ui/src/** (no kit change, except a script the count runs if the skill ships one)
change: (1) The fact count is a floor, not the check: after it prints nothing, the builder reads the page aloud, part by part, and writes in DESIGN.md one line per fact with every slot that says it; a value one helper prints into two parts, a label map entry shown in a status, a footer and a table, a state said by a caption, a pill and a sub line, and a legend that repeats an axis title each count as a repeat (n69 .5, n70 .14, n71 .19, n72 .28, n73 .38, n74 .44; X1 on 6 of 6). (2) Size each part to its content: a Heatmap takes `height` for few rows rather than `matchHeight` in a tall card (n69 .6), no `min-h` that outgrows the rows (n72 .29), `phone: 'columns'` for a list of ten or more numeric rows at 390 (n72 .29), footer `rows` on every strip cell so one tall cell leaves no band (n73 .39), and no tall card beside a column of two (n74 .45; X2 on 6 of 6). (3) The colour budget on a page of figures: a delta pill is `polarity: 'neutral'` unless its direction is the page's one status hue, a warn tone or dot beside a red and green pair is a second hue, and two accent lines told apart by dash alone need direct labels (n69 .2, n73 .33, n74 .42). (4) A part at a grain no focus arm reaches is folded into a part that joins or dropped: a per-account fact beside a cell grid is a `BarList` on `focusItems` (n69 .1); a daily chart of the wallets' children beside a table that takes one focus arm is joined or left out (n74 .46). (5) Name every item of a band axis at 390: `x.tickFormat` writes short ticks apart from the readout, and on a Heatmap `formatCol` returning '' thins ticks while `tickCols` only adds them (n70 .12, P2 cause; n69 .8). (6) A delta pill stands against a baseline the data holds and shows it: no 'vs yesterday' with no prior day, and a rate gap names both rates (n72 .23, n73 .32). (7) Single lessons, each a line where the builder reads it: a state a clause asks for is a word on its item through the bar `values` callback, not a second pane (n70 .9, .10); write every percent through `useFormat().percent`, one form per page (n71 .21); the noun a figure counts goes in `unit`, since `period` draws after the status (n72 .22); a `spread` series says it nudges, and the axis ends where the data ends (n72 .24, .31); a strip figure in an inset is `StatGroup variant="cards"` (n73 .40); a `Heatmap` needs stable accessors and data in a build without the compiler, which heatmap.d.ts names and the skill does not (n69 wish).
acceptance: The read-aloud pass is a required DESIGN.md section and names the four repeat shapes the count cannot see, with a worked example
